before: switch evaluates its controlling integer expression and starts at a matching case label or default.
After a matching case, statements continue into following labels unless control leaves. break exits this switch.
default supplies an optional path when no case value matches.
Removing break changes control flow, not just formatting. Use it only when falling through is a deliberate requirement.
Expected output or behavior: one. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Predict choice 1,2,and 9. Explain where break stops execution without relying on indentation. You may trace it without a C compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: `switch` checks an integer value. It starts at the case with that value. Here, choice selects which message to print.
`break` leaves the switch. Without it, work continues into the next case, even if that case's label does not match.
`default` is the place to start when no case matches. It is optional. Here it prints other.
Continuing from one case into the next is called fallthrough. Use it only when you want both pieces of work to run. Indentation alone does not stop it.
choice is 1, so the program starts at case 1. It prints one, then break leaves the switch.
Change choice to 2 and follow the matching case until break. The code before that matching case does not run.
